quests.textToSpeak: We're throwing a surprise party for her fortieth this weekend.
quests.textWithBlanks: We're throwing a surprise ___ for her fortieth this weekend.
quests.explanation: A surprise party, dinner and gathering are all plausible weekend plans, and each changes what the listener should expect. Party is short and unstressed at the end of the clause.
quests.hint: A get-together to mark someone's birthday.

quests.textToSpeak: Whatever you do, don't let her find out. Keep it a secret.
quests.textWithBlanks: Whatever you do, don't let her find out. Keep it a ___.
quests.explanation: Keep it a secret, quiet and hidden all mean don't tell her, but secret is the fixed phrase used with keep. Whatever you do at the front signals a serious warning.
quests.hint: To keep something a surprise by not telling the person.

quests.textToSpeak: Everyone's chipping in for a gift, if you want to join in.
quests.textWithBlanks: Everyone's chipping in for a ___, if you want to join in.
quests.explanation: Chip in for a gift, cost or present all describe pooling money together, and all three nouns fit after chip in for. Chip in is casual and extremely common among friends.
quests.hint: To organise something for a group with no single planner in charge.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I declined it, but I didn't really explain why.
quests.textWithBlanks: I ___ it, but I didn't really explain why.
quests.explanation: Declined, refused and rejected all describe saying no, but declined is the most conversational here alongside didn't explain why. Explaining why comes after, so wait for the full sentence.
quests.hint: Chose not to accept an offer.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Looking back, I think it probably sounded harsh, even though I didn't mean it that way.
quests.textWithBlanks: Looking back, I think it probably sounded ___, even though I didn't mean it that way.
quests.explanation: Sounded harsh, cold and dismissive all describe an unintended tone, and the speaker is regretting how it came across. Sounded is what someone else perceived, not what was meant.
quests.hint: In a way that hurt her feelings without meaning to.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I probably should apologise before it becomes a bigger thing.
quests.textWithBlanks: I probably should ___ before it becomes a bigger thing.
quests.explanation: Apologise, explain and reach out are three different ways of trying to fix a misunderstanding, and probably softens the intention into something tentative. I probably should is a mild, self-critical way of admitting a mistake.
quests.hint: To say sorry properly, in person or in words.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: If it happens again, you should escalate it to your senior manager.
quests.textWithBlanks: If it happens again, you should escalate it to your ___ manager.
quests.explanation: Senior manager, director and supervisor are all people you could escalate something to, and each sits at a slightly different level. Escalate it to is a formal phrase worth recognising in a workplace.
quests.hint: The manager above your immediate boss.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Before we go any further, can I just check one thing?
quests.textWithBlanks: Before we go any ___, can I just check one thing?
quests.explanation: Before we go any further, before we get started and before we finish all introduce a pause, but only one fits with talking about the next step. Go any further signals the speaker wants to slow things down.
quests.hint: The next stage that follows this one.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Just to make sure we're on the same page, can you repeat that back?
quests.textWithBlanks: Just to make sure we're on the same ___, can you repeat that back?
quests.explanation: On the same page, on the same team and in agreement all mean people understand each other, with on the same page being the most idiomatic. Just to make sure signals the speaker wants confirmation, not new information.
quests.hint: In agreement, with nothing contradicting each other.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Let me start with the positive feedback, and then we can talk about what needs work.
quests.textWithBlanks: Let me start with the ___ feedback, and then we can talk about what needs work.
quests.explanation: Positive feedback usually comes before criticism, and honest and clear could both describe the second half of a review. First introduces a sequence, so the listener knows more is coming.
quests.hint: You start with this before talking about anything difficult.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: There's definitely room for improvement when it comes to timekeeping.
quests.textWithBlanks: There's definitely room for ___ when it comes to timekeeping.
quests.explanation: Room for improvement, growth and development are three ways of softening criticism, and all three follow there's definitely. Definitely stresses the speaker's certainty despite the gentle tone.
quests.hint: Ways of getting better in the future.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Overall though, you've made genuinely great progress this year.
quests.textWithBlanks: ___ though, you've made genuinely great progress this year.
quests.explanation: Overall, generally and honestly are all natural openers for a summary, but overall specifically signals the whole picture rather than one part of it. Genuinely stresses that the praise is sincere, not routine.
quests.hint: In general, taking everything together.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: So, tell me a bit about your background before we get started.
quests.textWithBlanks: So, tell me a bit about your ___ before we get started.
quests.explanation: Background, education and experience are all things an interviewer might ask about, and each starts the interview a little differently. Tell me a bit about is the classic opening line of an interview.
quests.hint: The place where you have studied for your qualifications so far.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Can you tell me about a time you had to handle a difficult situation?
quests.textWithBlanks: Can you tell me about a time you had to handle a difficult ___?
quests.explanation: A time you had to handle a situation, solve a problem and lead a team are three separate interview questions with three separate answers to prepare. Can you tell me about a time is the standard opener for competency-based questions.
quests.hint: A difficult moment you had to manage under pressure.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Right, I think that covers everything. Any questions for us?
quests.textWithBlanks: Right, I think that covers everything. Any questions for ___?
quests.explanation: Any questions for us, us or for me are all natural at the close of an interview, and the choice tells you whether it is one person or a panel asking. This is almost always the final line of an interview.
quests.hint: Questions that you get to ask them, at the end.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I'm struggling a bit with the current module, to be honest.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'm struggling a bit with the current ___, to be honest.
quests.explanation: Struggling with the current module, chapter or unit are all realistic study problems, and each is a slightly different chunk of a course. Struggling with is a common, honest way for a student to open a request for help.
quests.hint: The stage of a course you are currently in.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Maybe it's worth booking a tutorial to go through it properly.
quests.textWithBlanks: Maybe it's worth booking a ___ to go through it properly.
quests.explanation: Book a tutorial, a session and a slot are all things students arrange, and each implies a slightly different kind of appointment. Tutorial is the standard word for one-on-one academic help.
quests.hint: A meeting where a tutor gives you individual feedback.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: If you submitted anything late, you'll need to email the department directly.
quests.textWithBlanks: If you ___ anything late, you'll need to email the department directly.
quests.explanation: Submitted late, missed and handed in late describe the same problem, but submitted late is the neutral, official version. Anything is a soft filler, and submitted arrives right after it.
quests.hint: Late, without permission, missing the cut-off.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I've been feeling a bit stressed lately, mainly because of work.
quests.textWithBlanks: I've been feeling a bit ___ lately, mainly because of work.
quests.explanation: Stressed, tired and overwhelmed all describe a difficult week, with stressed being the most common in this context. Been feeling a bit introduces something the speaker admits with some hesitation.
quests.hint: A feeling of pressure and worry about many small things.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Could you check when my next appointment is, please?
quests.textWithBlanks: Could you check when my next ___ is, please?
quests.explanation: Appointments, results and referrals are all things a surgery keeps a record of, and each fits naturally with the sentence. Appointments has that same extra syllable you met with messages and glasses.
quests.hint: The list of visits you have booked at the surgery.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: It's been on and off for a couple of weeks now.
quests.textWithBlanks: It's been ___ and off for a couple of weeks now.
quests.explanation: On and off, now and then, and off and on all describe an irregular pattern, and any could describe pain over several weeks. This kind of paired phrase is spoken as one fast unit.
quests.hint: Comes and goes, not steady or constant.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: The app's broken again, so I can't check my balance.
quests.textWithBlanks: The app's ___ again, so I can't check my balance.
quests.explanation: Broken, glitchy and slow are all realistic ways to describe an app misbehaving, and all three could plausibly explain a failed payment. Broken suggests something has properly stopped functioning.
quests.hint: Not working correctly at all right now.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: The support team's completely unreachable right now.
quests.textWithBlanks: The support team's completely ___ right now.
quests.explanation: Unreachable, offline and unavailable all describe someone you cannot contact, though they suggest slightly different reasons. Support team's is support team plus is squashed together before the adjective.
quests.hint: Not able to be reached by anyone.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: It kept rejecting my login details for some reason.
quests.textWithBlanks: It kept rejecting my ___ details for some reason.
quests.explanation: Login details, security answers and PIN numbers are three different things a system might reject, and each ending in -s makes the plural quick to miss. Kept rejecting suggests it happened more than once.
quests.hint: The details you need to enter to prove who you are.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: You'll never guess what. The neighbours complained about the party.
quests.textWithBlanks: You'll never guess what. The neighbours ___ about the party.
quests.explanation: The neighbours complained, cancelled and left all end the sentence differently, and only one word decides what actually happened. This is the classic structure of gossip: setup, then a surprising final detail.
quests.hint: The last thing you say before hanging up.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Honestly, the whole thing left me completely confused.
quests.textWithBlanks: Honestly, the whole thing left me completely ___.
quests.explanation: Left me completely confused, curious and annoyed are three different reactions to the same piece of news. Confused, curious and annoyed all begin with different sounds, so the front of the word carries the meaning here.
quests.hint: Not sure what is actually going on.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: I'll tell you the real story later on, it's a long one.
quests.textWithBlanks: I'll tell you the real ___ later on, it's a long one.
quests.explanation: The real story, truth and gossip are all things a friend might promise to explain, and each frames the conversation a little differently. Later on suggests the explanation is deliberately being delayed.
quests.hint: The truthful account of what really occurred.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: It turned out to be a lot smaller than expected, actually.
quests.textWithBlanks: It turned out to be a lot ___ than expected, actually.
quests.explanation: Turned out smaller, busier and shorter are three ways a wedding could have surprised the speaker, and turned out signals the reality differed from expectations. Than expected only makes sense after a comparative word.
quests.hint: Lower in scale than most people would have guessed.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Apparently the bride and groom decided to keep it fairly low-key.
quests.textWithBlanks: Apparently the bride and ___ decided to keep it fairly low-key.
quests.explanation: The bride and groom, hosts and organisers could all have decided to keep it low-key, and each shifts the responsibility for the decision. The bride and groom decided is a neutral way of reporting someone else's choice.
quests.hint: The two people getting married.
quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and select the word that accurately fills the blank.

quests.textToSpeak: Still, everyone said it was a lovely day.
quests.textWithBlanks: ___, everyone said it was a lovely day.
quests.explanation: Still, though and anyway all soften a following statement, but still most directly signals a contrast with what came before. This little word at the start of a clause is easy to drop entirely when listening.
quests.hint: Even so, despite what was just said.
